title: feat(lint,spec): warn on a user field whose reference names an object other than sys_user (18.x loud half; refusal is the next major's)
body:
Closes #24808

Clause-②: yes (widening)

The claim's `Clause-②: no` line was provisional. It is reset here, and in the changeset, from the measurement below. Under 「甲」 no conversion carries the refusal, so this PR is warning-only: no accept set narrows. It does publish one new rule id constant and its `os explain` entry from `@objectstack/lint`, and that is a widening of the public surface. That follows the lint precedent, where publishing rule-id constants was declared `yes (widening)`. The changeset is `minor` for `@objectstack/lint` and `patch` for `@objectstack/spec`.

## What this does

- **`@objectstack/lint`: new advisory `user-field-foreign-reference`.** It fires on a `user` field, on an object or an object extension, whose `reference` names an object other than `sys_user`. It is a warning on `os validate`, `os build` and `os lint` (through the reference-integrity suite in the authoring registry), so no command's exit code changes. The hint is the canonical spelling: `{ type: 'lookup', reference: 'TARGET' }`, or drop `reference`. `USER_FIELD_FOREIGN_REFERENCE` is exported from the barrel, and `RULE_EXPLANATIONS` gains its entry.
- **`@objectstack/spec`: `Field.user()`'s config types `reference` as `@deprecated`.** The accept set and the output are unchanged. The docblocks on `Field.user()` and `IMPLICIT_REFERENCE_TARGETS` now say what is declared and what is enforced.
- **In-repo producers.** One fixture was incidental and is now a `lookup`: `packages/lint/src/object-graph.test.ts`, the module fixture `owner`. Two pins of the 18.x resolution are kept on purpose, each with a comment: `packages/spec/src/data/field-value.test.ts` (`my_people`), and the object-graph "explicit carrier wins" control, which now builds its own inline fixture.

## Step 1: measuring producers (tree `objectstack-ai/objectstack` @ `b42c621c05`)

Scan: every object literal with `type: 'user'` (TS or JSON quoting, nested-brace-free) whose `reference` is not `'sys_user'` or `SystemObjectName.USER`, plus `Field.user({ … reference … })`, plus a window scan of six lines either side of 413 `type: 'user'` lines in 176 files.

| where | count | paths |
|---|---|---|
| `examples/**` (all example apps) | 0 | none |
| package source (non-test) | 0 | none |
| `Field.user({ reference })` calls | 0 | none (67 `Field.user(` lines, none pass `reference`) |
| test fixtures | 2 | `packages/spec/src/data/field-value.test.ts:91` (`my_people`), `packages/lint/src/object-graph.test.ts:39` (`crm_person`) |
| YAML | 0 | none |

The window scan's other 81 candidates were all neighbouring `lookup` fields or unreadable-carrier refusal probes (`reference: { object: 'sys_user' }`). Read by hand, none is a foreign-target `user`.

## Step 2: can an ADR-0087 conversion carry the refusal? No

ADR-0087 D2 scopes conversions to "losslessly mappable changes only". Rewriting `{ type: 'user', reference: X }` to `{ type: 'lookup', reference: X }` keeps the stored shape and every reader that follows the target. It changes three behaviours that are measured in this tree:

1. **Delete semantics: the blocker.** `user` is outside the referential delete walk. `DELETE_SEMANTICS_REFERENCE_TYPES` in `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` is `master_detail`, `lookup` and `tree`. `FieldSchema`'s overwrite materializes `deleteBehavior: 'set_null'` on `lookup` / `tree` only (`field.zod.ts`, the #9784 block). So today, deleting an X record leaves a `user(X)` column untouched. After the rewrite, it would null that column, and `planCascadeAtomicity` would plan X's deletes differently. `deleteBehavior` is `set_null | cascade | restrict`, and none of these means "do nothing". No rewrite preserves the behaviour.
2. **Sharing.** `fieldHoldsUsers` (`plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts`) answers true for any `user` field. After the rewrite it is false for a lookup to X.
3. **`current_user` default.** It is legal on `user` whatever the reference. On `lookup(X)` with X not `sys_user` it is refused at parse (`default-value-shape.ts`), so that subset would convert into a refused shape.

So under 「甲」 rule 2, 18.x ships the loud half only, and the refusal is filed for 19.0. The follow-up text is in the report for the seat.

## Step 3: what was not done in 18.x, and why

- **`referenceTargetOf` for `user` still returns the authored carrier.** Making it return `sys_user` would silently re-target a field that still loads (expand, import, seed and FK resolution would flip from X to `sys_user`). That is a behaviour change with no conversion and no refusal in front of it, which is what 「甲」 keeps out of an 18.x minor. It moves with the 19.0 refusal: once parse refuses a foreign carrier, the carrier can only ever be `sys_user`. The dispatch asked for this flip "either way". This PR does not make it, and the report records the deviation as an open question.
- **`Field.user()` is not type-narrowed to `reference?: 'sys_user'`.** That would be a compile-time refusal of the TS authoring surface with no conversion, so it is a 19.0 narrowing too. Keeping `...config` last is deliberate. Moving `reference: 'sys_user'` after the spread would silently re-target an untyped caller's field. With the spread last, the lint sees the foreign carrier and warns.

## Tests

Reproduction first: `ObjectSchema.safeParse({ name: 'probe_task', fields: { owner: { type: 'user', label: 'Owner', reference: 'probe_account' } } })` succeeds, and `referenceTargetOf` answers `probe_account`. The 18.x half pins that this shape still loads.

- New `describe('[#24808] …')` in `packages/lint/src/validate-object-references.test.ts`. It covers the warning (rule, severity, path, where, message, hint), object extensions, the map form, one-line message and hint of at most 200 characters, the `os explain` entry, and the authoring registry on `validate` / `build` / `lint` (advisory, never an error). Controls: no `reference`, `reference: 'sys_user'` and `Field.user()` stay silent; `Field.lookup('probe_account')` and a literal lookup stay silent; an unreadable carrier still throws.
- Ablation: `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` deleted the `findings.push(...userFieldForeignReferenceFindings(stack))` line (anchor 1 → 0, blob `bc1ff6a17b` → `3390aeb770`), and 7 tests went red. Restored with `git checkout HEAD`: the blob matched `HEAD:` (`bc1ff6a17b`) and `git diff HEAD` was empty. Lint tests import `src` directly, so no `dist` leg applies.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test`: 151 files / 7005 tests passed. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` exit 0. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/data`: 132 files / 4169 passed.
- Gates: At head `3815407620`, the derivation `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` gives 88 families. All ran, and `--ran` reconciles them: 86 exit 0, and 2 are NOT MEASURED. Those two are `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:lean-entry-closure`, each exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET: they read a full-monorepo `dist` this worktree did not build, so they are declared to CI. Also exit 0: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` (all 14 artifacts up to date), `check:adr-0087-registration` (no declared-breaking changeset), `check:changeset-no-major` and `check:nul-bytes`. Package `integration` tiers do not apply: the diff touches no CLI or driver spawn path.

## Acceptance notes

- objectui's checkout here is old (`b434f5f47`), and in it `packages/fields/src/__tests__/userCell.readGate-10535.test.tsx:157` renders `{ type: 'user', reference: 'crm_member' }`. That is a renderer fixture, not a metadata producer. Carrier: whoever lands the 19.0 refusal.
- No runtime publish-gate (Studio, REST `/meta`, MCP) object-write leg: the reference suite member runs on `flow` / `dataset` snapshots only. Crossing it onto `object` writes is that member's own false-positive measurement (its `runtimeTypes` docblock). Carrier: none.
